rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods <U+2013> two-season (2014, 2015) mini-lysimeter experiment in Karaj, Iran, comparing DI and SDI for forage corn, three replicates each. Q2: Table 4 and Results ('Variations in LAI... and WUE') <U+2013> WUE of corn was 8.32 kg/m3 under SDI versus 6.67 under DI (mean of two seasons), with SDI higher in each year. Q4: Table 2 and Methods <U+2013> soil evaporation measured with unplanted mini-lysimeters and transpiration derived; E was lower (157.6 vs 197.9 mm) and Tp higher under SDI, and ETc-act lower (384.8 vs 423.4 mm), which the authors use to explain the higher WUE.
rows.notes: Q3: single method (lysimeter water balance plus biomass harvest), no independent second method. Q5/Q6: one loamy site, one crop, mini-lysimeter plot scale within one farm. Q7: authors describe drier soil surface under SDI and buried line at 30 cm but do not state conditions required for the effect. Q8: only limitation stated concerns transferability of Kcb/Ke values across locations, not the WUE result. Q9: Table 4 gives means with LSD letter groupings only, no SD/CI.

rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods <U+2013> own two-season mini-lysimeter experiment comparing DI and SDI for corn.
rows.notes: The study reports no weed measurements or data. 'Low weed incidence' appears only in the abstract's Research highlights as an asserted contributor to SDI superiority; there is no weed variable in the methods, tables or figures. The study measured ETc-act, E, Tp, LAI, height, stem diameter, biomass and WUE only.

rows.evidence: Q1: Material and methods <U+2013> own two-season mini-lysimeter field experiment, DI vs SDI, three replicates. Q2: Table 4 and Results <U+2013> biomass yield was 81.90 t/ha under SDI versus 63.21 t/ha under DI (mean), significantly higher under SDI in both 2014 and 2015. Q4: Table 2, Table 4, Figs 3<U+2013>5 <U+2013> the authors measured the partitioning of ET into soil evaporation and transpiration (higher Tp and lower E under SDI) and LAI, height and stem diameter, which they use to explain the biomass advantage through better root-zone moisture and uptake.
rows.notes: Q3: one method only (harvest of mini-lysimeter plants). Q5/Q6: single site, soil, crop; plot/mini-lysimeter scale. Q7: no requirement conditions stated from own findings. Q8: no limitations stated for the yield result (mini-lysimeter scale, two seasons not discussed as restrictions). Q9: means with letter groupings only, no dispersion measure.

notes: Full text appears complete; equation (3) body is missing from the extraction but this does not affect the ratings. Experiment is at mini-lysimeter scale (40 cm diameter) embedded in an 18-ha farm, one loamy site, forage corn, two seasons.
